NONE: › written abbreviation for
avenue (ROAD)
› to do harm to or punish the person responsible for something bad done to you or your family or friends in order to achieve a fair situation
報…之仇，報復；為…雪恥，替…報仇

example: He swore he would avenge his brother's death.
他發誓要報殺兄之仇。
She determined to avenge herself on the killer.
她決心要讓兇手血債血償。
At the end of the film, the murderer is killed by his victim's avenging girlfriend.
電影的最後，受害者的女友終於報仇雪恨，殺死了兇手。

C: C1 a wide road with trees or tall buildings on both sides, or a wide country path or road with trees on both sides
（兩邊有樹或高樓的）大街；（鄉間寬闊的）林蔭大道
› UK a road that leads to a large house
C2 a method or way of doing something

example: Fremont Avenue
弗里蒙特大街
We should explore/pursue every avenue in the search for an answer to this problem.
我們應該嘗試一切途徑尋求該問題的答案。
Only two avenues are open to us - either we accept his offer or we give up the fight completely.
我們只有兩條路可走——要麼接受他的提議，要麼完全放棄鬥爭。
Synonym
possibility

NONE: › to say that something is certainly true
斷言；堅稱

example: The lawyer averred her client's innocence.
那名律師堅稱她的當事人無罪。
[ + speech ] "He's guilty, I tell you," she averred.
「我告訴你們，他有罪。」她一口咬定說。
[ + that ] She averred that he was guilty.
她一口咬定他有罪。

C or U: B1 [ C or U ] the result you get by adding two or more amounts together and dividing the total by the number of amounts

before noun: B1 [ before noun ] An average number is the number you get by adding two or more amounts together and dividing the total by the number of amounts.

S or U: B1 [ S or U ] a standard or level that is considered to be typical or usual
一般水準；一般水準；平均水準

NONE: › to reach a particular amount as an average
平均數是，平均為
A2 typical and usual
普通的；平常的；中等的；一般的

example: Prices have risen by an average of four percent over the past year.
物價在過去一年中上漲了4%。
My income's rather variable, but I earn £175 a day on average.
我的收入很不穩定，但是平均每天賺175英鎊。
The audience figures were lower than average for this sort of film.
對於這種類型的電影而言，這樣的觀眾人數是低於平均水準的。
In western Europe, a seven to eight-hour working day is about the average.
在西歐，一天工作七到八小時基本是平均水準。
On average, people who don't smoke are healthier than people who do.
一般而言，不抽煙的人比抽煙的人身體健康。
The quality of candidates was (well) below/above average.
這些候選人的素質（大大）低於／高於一般水準。
I expect to spend an average of $50 to $60 on a meal in a restaurant.
我去餐廳吃飯，一般一頓飯也就想花50到60英鎊。
Enquiries to our office average 1,000 calls a month.
我們辦公室每個月平均接到1000個詢問電話。
Many doctors average (= work an average of) 70 hours a week.
很多醫生每週平均工作70個小時。
Trainee accountants average (= earn an average of) £32,000 per year.
實習會計師平均每年收入32 000英鎊。

NONE: › to be or become equal in amount or number
數量相當，達到平衡

example: The highs and lows of life tend to average out in the end.
人生一世，往往起起落落，到頭來還算公道。

NONE: › to have a particular number or amount as the average
算出的平均值是，平均為

example: My annual holiday varies, but it averages out at five weeks a year.
我每年的假期時間長短不等，但是平均算來是每年5週。

NONE: › to calculate the average of a set of numbers or amounts
算出…的平均數
› strongly disliking or opposed to
反對的；嫌惡的；不願意的

example: Few people are averse to the idea of a free holiday.
幾乎沒有人會反對免費假期這個主意。
I'm not averse to (= I like) the occasional glass of champagne myself.
我樂得偶爾自己來一杯香檳。

NONE: › (a person or thing that causes) a feeling of strong dislike or of not wishing to do something
厭惡，反感；討厭的人（或事物）

example: I felt an instant aversion to his parents.
我立刻對他的父母產生了反感。
She has a deep aversion to getting up in the morning.
早上她很不願意起床。
Greed is my pet aversion (= the thing I dislike most of all).
我最痛恨貪得無厭。

NONE: › a method of treating habits or types of behaviour that are not wanted or not acceptable, by causing the patient to connect them with bad feelings
厭惡療法（引起患者對自己的有害習慣或行為的厭惡，以達到戒除目的）

example: Despite what many people think, aversion therapy is no longer used by professional psychologists in this country.
與很多人所認為的相反，這個國家的專業心理學家已經不再採用厭惡療法了。

NONE: › making someone feel a strong dislike for something, or making them not want to do it
厭惡的，反感的
› Aversive methods of stopping someone from behaving in a particular way involve doing something unpleasant to that person whenever they do something you do not want them to do.
厭惡療法的

example: emotionally aversive images
令人心生厭惡的圖像

T: › to prevent something bad from happening
› to turn away your eyes or thoughts
轉移（目光、想法等）；把…轉（向別處）

example: to avert a crisis/conflict/strike/famine
避免危機／衝突／罷工／饑荒
to avert disaster/economic collapse
防止災難／經濟崩潰
Synonym
avoid
I averted my gaze/eyes while he dressed.
他穿衣服的時候，我把目光轉向一邊。
We tried to avert our thoughts from our massive financial problems.
我們盡量不去想我們面臨的嚴重財政問題。
